Subject: Post-call: model routing / policy requirements

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope the integration work: 

1) Goals
- Low single-digit token latency for user-facing chat (SLO: 150-200ms p95)
- Aggressive cost target for background processing (embeddings + reranking)

2) Integration items we want to validate
- SDK setup and auth options (API key, mTLS, or SSO for internal service-to-service)
- Model routing: prefer low-latency variants for chat, cost-optimized fallbacks for bulk jobs
- Structured output / tool calling: need deterministic JSON output for downstream processors
- Embeddings & reranker flow: batch embedding jobs and a separate reranker model for top-N re-ranking

3) Constraints
- Data residency: US-only region for PII workflows
- Procurement timeline: want an initial PO within 6 weeks if scope matches

I attached our initial requirements workbook (acme-reqs.xlsx). Can we get a short technical deep-dive next week to walk SDK/auth options and a demo of routing policies (fallback chains, region routing)?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Alex — great summary, thanks. Really helpful to have the SLO and cost constraints upfront.

Short answers and proposed next steps: 

- SDK & auth: Redwood SDK supports API keys today; we also support mTLS for dedicated/private customers and SSO via OIDC for admin/console access. For service-to-service we typically recommend short-lived API keys (rotate via your KMS) or mutual TLS for higher security. I attached our integration guide with code snippets.

- Model routing & policies: we can configure routing policies by latency target, cost budget, and region. Fallback chains are supported — e.g., primary low-latency model (quantized) -> fallback to standard model -> fallback to cheaper batched variant for background jobs. I attached an example YAML (routing-policy-example.yaml) showing a sample chain.

- Structured output & tool calling: we have a structured-output helper in the SDK that enforces JSON schema and validation. We can demo tool-calling and function invocations in the deep dive.

Proposed next steps:
1) 60-minute technical deep-dive with your platform team (include your security contact) — options: Wed 8/4 10am PT or Thu 8/5 9am PT.
2) Share any additional compliance questions (SOC2, audit logs) so we can pull evidence.
3) Draft routing policy based on your workload (we'll send a first-pass YAML).

I’ve cc'd Marcus (solutions lead) to join the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf, routing-policy-example.yaml

Subject: Re: Post-call: model routing / policy requirements — technical notes

Adding a few technical notes we should cover in the deep-dive: 

- Auth patterns
  * Short-lived API tokens minted via your KMS + rotation (good balance of ops & security)
  * mTLS when you want zero-trust mutual auth (recommended for Dedicated/Private)
  * OIDC for console/admin flows, not for per-request latency-critical service calls

- SDK setup
  * SDK has a small footprint (<200KB) and supports streaming responses and structured-output validation.
  * We can demonstrate live sample for function/tool calling and JSON schema enforcement.

- Model routing policy primitives (what we'll demo)
  * selectors: latency_target_ms, cost_budget_per_1000_tokens, region, model_family
  * actions: route_to_model, adjust_temperature, enable_batched_mode, load_balance_across_pool
  * fallback: ordered list of compatible variants; automatic re-eval if p95 latency breaches SLO

- Embedding/reranker pattern
  * Synchronous single-record embeddings for real-time requires different instance sizing vs batched bulk jobs
  * Recommend separate routing rules for embeddings queue -> batch GPU pool with cheaper quantized models; reranker stays on a CPU-optimized instance or smaller GPU depending on throughput

I'll prepare a short example policy and sample SDK snippet for Wed/Thu.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
